title: Good decision: events_handler lives in kithd, not in kith-events
description:
Decision: The events_handler HTTP handler is defined in kithd/src/events.rs, not in the kith-events crate. kith-events only exports the minimal channel creation function.

Code location: kithd/src/events.rs (the entire events_handler function and its tests).

Why this is correct: The handler owns HTTP/Axum concerns (extractors, request/response types, SSE encoding), auth checks (WhoIsProvider), and access to kithd-specific state (AppState). Putting the handler in kithd prevents kith-events from depending on Axum, auth infrastructure, or the daemon's request context. kith-events stays a lean event-infrastructure library: just channel setup and types.

The wrong alternative would be to place events_handler in kith-events. This would force kith-events to import and depend on Axum, the auth layer, and kithd's state types. It would bloat the library with HTTP concerns and couple the event library to the specific daemon architecture. Any change to auth or request handling would ripple through kith-events.

This is proper separation of concerns: infrastructure (channels) in the library, handler logic (HTTP/auth/state) in the daemon.
